extracted.intended_audience: Ministers, elders, and members of Reformed Presbyterian / Covenanter communities (readers of the Church's Judicial Testimony)
extracted.subtask_description: A doctrinal/judicial testimony enumerating grounds for testifying against other church bodies and explaining the standards by which faithfulness to the covenanted reformation is judged. It lists principles, procedural expectations, and examples of failures that warrant protest or exclusion from fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin warranted by scripture
rubrics_metrics.description: Their very origin was unwarranted by scripture; they made a breach without a definite object and multiply divisions in the visible body of Christ without necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizing a new church is illegitimate if it simply invites former brethren to join under the pretense of charity while in effect imposing a tyrannical new term of communion. Questions to ask: What iniquity is claimed against the old body? Are differences mere 'trifles' or essential principles 'sealed by the precious blood of martyrs'? Avoid secession that cannot justify itself scripturally and morally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of solemn covenants and covenanting practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Although covenanting was declared an 'important duty,' this body never recognized the solemn deeds of their fathers as binding on them nor attempted public, social covenanting competently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denying the obligation of the British covenants from pulpit and press, or ridiculing them, is a mark of unfaithfulness. The moral nature of covenanting, tied to prophetic declarations, demonstrates its permanency until the end of the world; parties should acknowledge and practice their fathers' covenant deeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper view of church fellowship (opposition to fixed/occasional communion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel distinction between 'fixed' and 'occasional' communion tends to catholic communion and undermines steadfastness of fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental/occasional communion leads to merging with other communions and loss of distinctive testimony. Ministers who advocate occasional communion or occupy pulpits interchangeably are evidencing latitudinarian tendencies that threaten covenantal fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound doctrine of the divine ordinance of civil government
rubrics_metrics.description: This church has been unsound on the doctrine of the divine ordinance of civil government, evidenced by the practice of her members mirroring that of Seceders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Churches must hold and teach a biblically consistent doctrine of magistracy and government; practical conformity to errant civic models signals doctrinal failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of boundless toleration and supremacy of individual conscience over Scripture
rubrics_metrics.description: The body has advocated a boundless toleration, assigning a sphere to conscience incompatible with due subjection to the Holy Scriptures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conscience must be subject to Scripture; ecclesiastical constitutions or 'constitutions' that give conscience an immunity from divine control are considered impious. Beware constitutions (e.g., titled 'Constitution of the Associate Reformed Church') that imply civil-republican models of conscience supremacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of the divine right and unalterableness of Presbyterian Church Government
rubrics_metrics.description: This church shuns declaring the divine right and unalterableness of Presbyterial Church Government and does not testify against Prelacy or Independency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a church claims Presbyterian practice but will not assert its divine right, it is on the same footing as the Revolution Church of Scotland. True fidelity requires explicit testimony for Presbyterian government and opposition to Prelacy/Independency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarding purity of divine worship in terms of fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: The purity of divine worship is not guarded: although 'No Hymns merely of human composure, are allowed,' the use of qualifying words ('merely', 'churches') renders the prohibition ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice reveals ministers who sing 'hymns merely of human composure' in other pulpits or allow congregational choice in worship — both signs of latitudinarianism. Terms of fellowship must clearly and practically exclude human-composed hymns if that is the intended standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain strict ecclesiastical discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Laxity of discipline is observable: admission to fellowship of persons who deny the divine warrant for a fast in connection with the Lord's Supper, ridicule parts of solemnity, habitually neglect family worship, and failure to enjoin fellowship meetings for prayer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission and participation in the seals of the covenant should be refused to those who openly deny established practices or neglect family/fellowship duties. Discipline must enforce covenantal practice and rites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary organization or multiplication of fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization of dissenting bodies was uncalled for where no new scriptural attainment was embraced that did not already exist under a judicial banner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separations prompted by harsh treatment or temporary impulse rather than principled constitutional defects are criticized; multiplication of separate fellowships is not a happy expedient for attaining union in truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent application of principles respecting magistracy and office-holding
rubrics_metrics.description: It is inconsistent to declare a civil constitution so immoral that no Christian can accept office under it, yet claim the privilege to choose others to fill those offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrinal positions on magistracy must be applied consistently. Attempts to separate legal obligations between representative and constituents (i.e., allow constituents to serve while dissuading personal service) are condemned as undermining covenants and moral government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and sobriety in teaching the doctrine of faith and assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctions and caveats relative to 'assurance' that 'darken counsel by words without knowledge' and tend toward 'vain jangling' are disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pastors and teachers should avoid confusing, subtle distinctions that bewilder lay readers; teaching on receiving and resting on Christ should aim at clear appropriation and assurance, not needless hair-splitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of intercommunion with corrupt communities
rubrics_metrics.description: A disposition to intercommunion—occupying pulpits with more corrupt communities, sharing the Lord's Supper, and co-operating in conventional proceedings with 'Reformed Churches'—is inconsistent with steadfastness and declared toleration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministers and members should not participate in sacraments or ordinations that violate Presbyterian order (e.g., one minister and ruling elders setting apart candidates); such practices indicate a departure from covenanted standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to censure and rebuke within the household of faith
rubrics_metrics.description: Charity which 'rejoiceth in the truth' requires Christ's witnesses to censure and rebuke those of the household of faith who are in course of error or sin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public, candid, and honest testimony against backsliders and those causing truth to be evil spoken is presented as necessary for reclaiming backsliders, confirming the wavering, and directing sincere inquirers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain covenantal separation from immoral civil institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawing dissent that embraces civil institutions (e.g., incorporating with the National Society) subverts the covenanted system of doctrine and order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joining national organizations whose terms are opposed to godliness and honesty is seen as entering a course subversive of covenantal doctrine; churches must avoid such political/civic entanglements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid clandestine seduction and undue influence in drawing disciples
rubrics_metrics.description: The party was charged with clandestinely exerting influence to seduce and draw away disciples for years, evidenced by petitions and correspondence connected to the defection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secret maneuvers, covert organizing, and influencing votes/petitions are improper ways to create a faction; openness and honor are required in matters of separation and organizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for and preservation of the Judicial Testimony and Terms of Communion
rubrics_metrics.description: This party is chargeable with mutilating the Judicial Testimony and changing the terms of communion, obtruding a mutilated formula contrary to due order; history and argument were excluded from terms of fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional or confessional documents should not be altered, expunged, or remodeled without proper overture to the people and due order. Removing historical parts (e.g., the Auchensaugh Covenant) or supplying mutilated formulas on unsuspecting people is condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include history and argument as part of the Church's Testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: History and argument were understood by the authors' fathers to constitute testimony; excluding uninspired history from bonds of fellowship is a practice of innovators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Testimony should embody both historical providences and doctrinal argument. Rejecting uninspired history from the confession or terms of fellowship is seen as inconsistent and self-contradictory with claims to follow the footsteps of the Scottish Reformers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not cooperate with immoral civil governments or connive with such practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Public fame charges certain Synods with connivance at members cooperating with the immoral and anti-Christian government of Great Britain; opening doors in their new Testimony for such confederacies is criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synods and churches must be vigilant against practices that give power to anti-Christian civil authorities. If Testimonies or prefaces effectively exclude doctrinal condemnation of such civil systems, beware of covert accommodation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid participation in popular benevolent associations when they depart from covenanted uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: Involvement in Sunday Schools, Bible Societies, Temperance Reforms, Missionary Enterprise, etc., is cited as evidence of departure from covenanted uniformity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement with popular benevolent movements must be judged by whether they align with covenanted testimony and uniformity; indiscriminate participation is viewed as corrupting and inconsistent with covenantal attainments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑clandestine and honorable formation of protest instruments and leagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruments like the 'Safety League' that had clandestine origins (framed and subscribed by those yet in fellowship) are lamented as dishonorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents, leagues, and reform measures should originate openly and honorably. Secret formation by those still in fellowship is an improper way to seek reform and compromises integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unwarrantable separation; maintain settled and consistent standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Some who declined Synod authority (1838) did so out of impulse rather than constitutional defects and lacked intelligence to manage consistent testimony; their paper interpreted inconsistently and covered only selective symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those separating must have settled standards and justifiable reasons; withdrawing without assigning justifiable reasons or maintaining no consistent standard is reprehensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural fairness in Synodical governance: permit petitions and full hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Synod refused to permit petitions, misrepresented respectful papers as 'abusive,' stopped petitioners from being heard, and shuffled important matters aside as mere 'letters.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts should allow petitions, memorials, and papers to be read and considered; silencing petitioners or misclassifying important petitions to avoid scrutiny is tyrannical and unjust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid synod packing and electioneering; secure legitimate court composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'packed Synod' composed chiefly of ministers and elders favoring innovations, and exclusion of those disposed to resist defection, facilitated introduction of error and tyranny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elections and delegate ratios must be honestly observed; manipulating court composition to achieve desired policies is dishonest and harmful to the church's witness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure due process and the right to vindication in disciplinary cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances cited where individuals (e.g., James McKinney, Miss King) were not allowed to read vindications or have their cases heard; members were interrupted or silenced improperly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary processes must allow accused or censured persons to present vindication and justification. Preventing hearing or silencing defendants is condemned as cruelty and violation of ordination vows and Presbyterian government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse confederation with the enemies of God; heed historic testimonies and warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of confederating with the enemies of God and resisting evidence from Scripture and historic witnesses is explicitly condemned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Councils must receive and heed testimonies, historic vindications, and writings (Cloud of Witnesses, Gillespie on Confederacies, etc.). Persisting in confederation despite such warnings is grounds for testimony against a body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fostering schism for carnal ends; pursue biblical unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Fostering schism for carnal ends—resulting in multiple Synods in organic fellowship but little ministerial or sacramental communion—is an indictment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schism that arises from selfish or worldly motives harms the church's witness and leads to sin and hardening of the profane; unity must be pursued on covenantal and scriptural grounds, not by factional interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate civil constitutions by Christian standards before giving allegiance
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States Constitution is criticized for lacking acknowledgment of the Christian religion, admitting Jews, Mohammedans, Deists, and Atheists to honors and emoluments, and establishing slavery; thus no Christian can consistently give allegiance to the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nations and constitutions should be judged as proper subjects of God's government; where a civil constitution contains moral evils of sufficient magnitude, Christian allegiance is questioned and testimony against such systems is incumbent.
